samples.text:
The graph shows the number of mobile phone subscriptions and landline subscriptions for every 100 people in one country between 1995 and 2025.

In 1995, landline was much more popular than mobile phone. There were 48 landline subscriptions per 100 people but only 6 mobile phone subscriptions. The landline went up a little to 52 in 2000, but after that it started to decrease. It was 42 in 2010 and 24 in 2020, and in 2025 it was only 17.

On the other hand, mobile phone subscriptions increased very fast. It was 38 in 2000 and 82 in 2005, so it became more than landline in this period. In 2010 it was 110, that means there were more mobile phones than people. After 2010 it continued to increase but more slowly, and it reached to 131 in 2025.

Overall, mobile phones became very popular and landlines became less popular. In the beginning landline was higher, but at the end mobile phone was much more higher than landline.
samples.why: Overview present but placed at the end and repetitive · key features including the crossover covered · limited vocabulary · pronoun agreement, preposition and double comparative errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The line graph compares the number of mobile phone and landline subscriptions per 100 people in a particular country over a thirty-year period from 1995 to 2025.

Overall, mobile phone subscriptions rose dramatically and overtook landlines early in the period, while landline subscriptions declined after an initial small increase. By the end of the period, there were far more mobile subscriptions than landline ones.

In 1995, landlines were clearly more common, with 48 subscriptions per 100 people compared with only 6 for mobile phones. Landline subscriptions reached their peak of 52 in 2000, but then fell steadily, dropping to 33 in 2015 and to just 17 by 2025, about a third of their highest level.

Mobile phone subscriptions, on the other hand, grew extremely rapidly in the first fifteen years. They reached 38 in 2000 and overtook landlines at some point between 2000 and 2005, when the figure had risen to 82. By 2010 the number had exceeded 100 per 100 people, meaning there were more subscriptions than people. After this, the growth has slowed down, with the figure reaching 131 in 2025.
samples.why: Clear overview including the crossover · key features logically presented · good cohesive range · appropriate vocabulary · frequent error-free sentences with one tense slip.

samples.text:
The graph tracks mobile phone and landline subscriptions per 100 people in one country between 1995 and 2025.

The two forms of telephone service moved in opposite directions. Mobile subscriptions expanded rapidly, overtaking landlines in the early 2000s and eventually exceeding the size of the population, whereas landline subscriptions, after peaking in 2000, fell steadily for the remainder of the period.

At the beginning of the period, landlines were far more widespread, with 48 subscriptions per 100 people against a mere 6 for mobiles. Landline numbers rose marginally to 52 in 2000 but declined thereafter, gradually at first and then more sharply, dropping to 33 in 2015 and to just 17 by 2025, less than a third of their peak.

Mobile subscriptions, by contrast, soared in the first decade, climbing to 38 in 2000 and then to 82 in 2005, by which point they had clearly surpassed landlines. Growth continued strongly until 2010, when the figure reached 110, meaning subscriptions outnumbered people. From then on, growth slowed markedly, with the rate increasing only modestly to 124 in 2015 and 131 in 2025.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including the crossover and later levelling off · clear, well-placed overview · accurate figures and derived fraction · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures.
